name: The five kings at Makkedah
charge: Confederating against Gibeon for making peace with Israel
summary: Five Amorite kings joined to punish Gibeon for coming to terms with Joshua. Israel came up all night from Gilgal, the Lord cast great stones from heaven on them, and the sun stood still. The five fled into a cave at Makkedah. Joshua had great stones rolled on the mouth of it and posted men, finished the battle, and then brought them out, had the captains put their feet on their necks, and hanged them on five trees until evening.
offense: The attack was on Gibeon rather than on Israel (Joshua 10:1), and Gibeon's only offense was making peace. The record gives their motive as fear, because Gibeon was a great city and the men of it mighty (Joshua 10:2), and states the aggression plainly: they came up and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it. Israel was bound by an oath to defend the city, an oath obtained by deceit and entered separately in this volume, so the campaign is Israel keeping a covenant it had been tricked into.
judgment: The Lord discomfited them, and more died from the hailstones than Israel killed with the sword (Joshua 10:11). They were taken alive from the cave, and the treading on their necks was done in front of the army with the words spoken over it, fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage, for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies (Joshua 10:25). They were hanged on five trees and taken down at sundown (Joshua 10:26), which is Deuteronomy 21 kept exactly in the middle of a war, and the stones that had shut them in the cave were rolled back over their bodies (Deuteronomy 21:22-23).
